name: Titanic
label: Unheard of Hope
lede: A Guatemalan cellist and a Mexico City guitarist-producer who make records the way other people renovate a house: room by room, pop in one, black metal in the next.

eras.title: A cellist leaves the church
eras.text: Mabe Fratti grows up in Guatemala in a Pentecostal household where the only approved music is Christian and classical. The cello is the one thing that carries over when she walks out of the church.

years.h: A Goethe Institute residency drops Fratti in Mexico City
years.p: [[Mabe Fratti|ddefada4-c07e-43d3-9837-318805f37776]], born in Guatemala in 1992 and trained on cello, arrives on a Goethe Institute residency and stays for the city's improvising scene.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Fratti grew up in a Pentecostal household, studied classical cello, and widened her listening through file-sharing, a György Ligeti record her father brought home and a Jacqueline du Pré DVD she found in a shop. After leaving the church as a teenager she started pushing reggae, blues and funk through the cello.

In Mexico City she worked with players including Libertad Figueroa, Gudrun Gut and Julián Bonequi, and met [[Héctor Tosta|1e57c09c-5d04-4df1-916a-1e806e4a2f27]], the future other half of Titanic, along with the musicians who became the collective [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]].

eras.title: Solo records, and a scene forming around her
eras.text: Before Titanic exists, Fratti builds a solo catalogue of cello records that move from chamber quiet to something louder. Coverage from The Guardian and Pitchfork follows.

years.h: Pies Sobre La Tierra, a debut built around a Sebald book
years.p: Fratti's first album takes its inspiration from W.G. Sebald's The Rings of Saturn.

years.h: Será Que Ahora Podremos Entendernos puts cello beside synths and field sound
years.p: The Guardian reviewed Fratti's second album in May 2021 as "soundscaped cello, synths and nature"; Pitchfork covered it too.

years.h: Se Ve Desde Aquí gets a rave from Oneohtrix Point Never
years.p: [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]] called Fratti's third album "mind blowing", and the record turned her from a Mexico City name into a European festival act.
years.xp:
Wikipedia quotes Daniel Lopatin's "mind blowing" verdict on Se Ve Desde Aquí, and The Guardian reviewed it in September 2022 as cathartic, powerful experimentation. The Locomotion, a Brussels radio show, later had her on to talk about the record, her Café Oto residency and the Mexican capital's alternative scene.

Lopatin's ear matters later: three years on he ends up playing on Titanic's second album.

eras.title: Titanic sails
eras.text: Tosta, who makes records as I. la Católica, and Fratti stop being collaborators on each other's projects and become a band with a name. Both keep their day jobs, Fratti's solo career and the wider Mexico City circle around them.

years.h: Vidrio: eight songs of chamber pop and jazz, Titanic's debut
years.p: Recorded across three Mexico City studios (Tinho, Progreso Nacional, Pedro y el Lobo) and released by Unheard of Hope.
years.xp: Our Culture's announcement lists the eight tracks: "Anónima", "Circulo Perfecto", "Cielo Falso", "Hotel Elizabeth", "En Paralelo", "Te evite", "Palacio" and "Balanza". Two of them, "Anónima" and "Hotel Elizabeth", came out ahead of the album. Beats Per Minute put it in its top 50 albums of 2023, and The Guardian's review called the pair a joyous Mexico City duo unbounded by genre.

years.h: A hotel in Bratislava names the record and shoots its cover
years.p: Titanic recorded "Hotel Elizabeth" in the Bratislava hotel that gave the song its title and the album its cover image.
years.xp: The video, directed by José Ostos, runs on surreal and unsettling imagery. Fratti told Our Culture that her voice sits "super relaxed" in the song's key and that she was thinking of Chet Baker's smooth delivery.

years.h: Amor Muere, Fratti's Mexico City collective, releases its album
years.p: [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]] (Fratti, Concepción Huerta, Gibrana Cervantes, Camille Mandoki) put out A Time to Love, a Time to Die.

years.src: Metacritic: Sentir Que No Sabes · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Fratti goes solo again with Sentir Que No Sabes
years.p: Metacritic lists a Metascore of 86 from 10 reviews, all positive, and a perfect 100 from The Guardian.
years.xp:
Metacritic lists the release date as June 28, 2024 and the label as Revolver USA. The Skinny said she uses "her cello, or some out-of-nowhere sonic texture, to constantly colour outside the lines".

Pitchfork had run a profile that March titled "Chasing the Goblin With Mabe Fratti, the Guatemalan Cellist at the Heart of Mexico City's Avant-Rock Scene", a reference Wikipedia gives.

eras.title: HAGEN
eras.text: Titanic take the pop-adjacent debut and blow the doors off: a New York studio, two producers, one guest synth player who wanted in, and and a European tour that ran from late August into October.

years.h: "La dueña" begins backstage at a Ben Howard show
years.p: Tosta found the chord progression warming up before a Ben Howard show in Austria, then dreamed the song into a heartbroken old lady betrayed by love.
years.xp: Tosta told Beats Per Minute the idea grew on the flight back to Mexico, and that karaoke nights at a Mexico City bar pushed him to try a full-hearted ballad. The video borrows telenovela looks.

years.h: "Gotera" comes out of a residency in the Netherlands
years.p: The lead single, announced with the album by Stereogum, began as material for a commission at a venue in Den Bosch.
years.xp: The band described the song as about "keeping up and moving forward as everything around us is on fire", per Stereogum. Drummer Eli Keszler improvises percussion toward the record's close.

q: Sometimes there's ideas that he would love and I'm like 'no, no, no.'
years.src: Metacritic: Hagen · Album of the Year: HAGEN · Album of the Year: Pitchfork · Paste · BOMB · Treble
years.p: Pitchfork scored the record 7.7 (Metacritic lists it as 77) and later ranked it No. 19 on its 50 best albums of 2025; The Guardian placed it No. 24.
years.xp:
Metacritic's summary of Pitchfork's review: "The music on HAGEN isn't impenetrable, though it is gargantuan." Other scores it lists: The Guardian 100, Paste 85 (Devon Chodzin) and Mojo 60. Album of the Year also lists Spectrum Culture at 68, and puts the critic average at 78 from five reviews.

BOMB heard black metal, drone, pedal steel, chamber pop and power ballads in the mix. Treble's Jeff Terich, reviewing it, quoted Fratti on the process: "sometimes there's ideas that he would love and I'm like 'no, no, no.'" Treble credits the label as Tin Angel/Unheard of Hope; Metacritic and Album of the Year say Unheard of Hope.

years.h: Oneohtrix Point Never hears the tapes and asks to play
years.p: [[Daniel Lopatin|d5cd6528-3185-4f1b-a297-807b00b16f83]] recorded synths on "Pájaro de fuego" during the final stretch of recording.
years.xp: According to FLOOD, HAGEN was recorded at Circular Ruin in New York with producers Nate Salon and [[Randall Dunn|f2be6d74-fac1-4199-9ddc-f3f280630994]]. Dunn tweaked an effects rack on the drums, adding gated reverb that Tosta and Fratti say lifted the groove of "Libra". Salon sampled Keszler's drums for "Gallina degollada".
